response.passage: Sports injuries are common, but knowing how to handle them is vital for recovery. A sprain involves damage to ligaments, which connect bones, while a strain occurs when muscles or tendons are overstretched. If you suffer an injury, the RICE method is the gold standard for immediate care. This means you should Rest the area, apply Ice wrapped in a cloth for short periods, Compress the injury with a bandage, and Elevate it above the level of your heart to reduce swelling. Never apply heat to a fresh injury, as this increases blood flow and worsens swelling. Furthermore, do not massage a new injury, as this can cause further tissue damage. Some injuries, like fractures, may not always look bent or deformed, so you must seek medical help if pain persists even if you can still move the limb. Most importantly, head injuries are serious. A concussion is a brain injury that may not show symptoms immediately. If a player receives a blow to the head, they must stop playing immediately and be assessed by a professional. Even if a player feels fine or says their headache has gone, they must not return to the game, as the brain needs time to heal fully. A helmet reduces the risk of injury but does not make a player completely immune to concussions.
response.summary: Properly managing sports injuries involves using the RICE method and avoiding heat or massage on fresh wounds. Head injuries require immediate removal from play because concussions are brain injuries that need time to heal.
